gloss: to come apart at the seams; to begin to bloom; to break into a smile

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: ほころびませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: ほころんでいなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: ほころんでいませんでした

definitions.gloss: to come apart at the seams; to come undone; to rip open
definitions.explanation: Stitching or fabric begins to split open or unravel. The original, literal meaning of the word.

definitions.gloss: to begin to bloom; to start to open (of flower buds)
definitions.explanation: Flower buds begin to open, showing the first signs of blooming. A poetic and commonly used sense.

definitions.gloss: to break into a smile; to soften (of one's expression)
definitions.explanation: A face or expression relaxes and a smile naturally emerges. Often used for a gentle, involuntary smile.

examples.english: My mother's face broke into a smile when she heard the news of my passing.

notes:
A beautiful word that connects three meanings through the image of something gently opening: seams splitting, buds blooming, and faces softening into smiles. Can also be written {綻|ほころ}ぶ in kanji, though hiragana is more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ほころぶ — to break into a smile
- ⟦{蕾|つぼみ}→蕾：04368_tsubomi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ほころぶ — buds begin to open
- ⟦{縫|ぬ}い{目|め}→縫い目：07102_nuime⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ほころぶ — a seam comes apart
- ⟦{表情|ひょうじょう}→表情：03585_hyoujou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ほころぶ — one's expression softens

USAGE:
Senses 2 and 3 are the most common in modern Japanese. The word has a gentle, poetic quality. Sense 3 specifically describes a natural, involuntary smile — not a deliberate grin. Often used with ⟦{思|おも}わ→思う：00492_omou⟧ず (involuntarily).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{咲|さ}く→咲く：08150_saku⟧ — to bloom (more general; ほころぶ emphasizes the very beginning of blooming)
- ほほえむ — to smile (neutral; ほころぶ emphasizes the involuntary, natural quality of the smile)
